lines.text: Do you know how a smoke alarm smells smoke? Many of them use a tiny bit of radiation to do it.
Inside is a small chamber with a speck of a material called americium. It gives off tiny particles that knock electrons off the air.
Those charged bits of air let a small electric current flow across the chamber, all day, every day.
When smoke drifts in, the particles stick to the smoke instead. The current drops, and the alarm goes off.
Other alarms use light. A beam shines across a dark chamber, and smoke scatters it onto a sensor.
The radiation is tiny and stays inside the case. You get more from the natural world around you.
Test it every month, and change it about every ten years.
So a smoke alarm is a tiny circuit, waiting for the air to change.
